D: Logan travels to Japan to say goodbye to a man he once saved and gets caught up in a family fight.
P: Serve the snacks when Logan fights on top of the bullet train.
S: the fight on top of the bullet train
Sushi rice shaped into triangles around flaked salted salmon, wrapped in strips of nori and packed into a bento box with pickled ginger.
Chicken thigh pieces threaded onto skewers, grilled and basted with soy, mirin and sugar simmered down until sticky, scattered with spring onion.
Pork and cabbage gyoza pan-fried until crisp underneath, steamed with a splash of water, with soy and rice vinegar to dip.
M: hiding out in the snowy mountain village
Ramen noodles in a rich pork and miso broth with slices of braised pork belly, soft-boiled eggs and spring onion.
Salmon fillets glazed with soy, mirin and sugar, grilled until sticky, served with steamed rice and a quick pickled cucumber salad.
W: the quiet gardens of the Yashida estate
Vanilla ice cream softened slightly, matcha powder whisked through, refrozen an hour and scooped into small bowls.
K: the funeral and the long night after
Sake warmed gently in a jug of hot water, poured into small cups, or green tea for anyone not drinking.

s.note: the fight on top of the bullet train
s.how: Cook 2 cups sushi rice. Salt and grill 200g salmon, then flake. Shape rice into triangles around a little salmon, wrap the base in nori and sprinkle with sesame. Pack into a bento box with pickled ginger for the train.

Simmer 4 tbsp soy sauce, 4 tbsp mirin and 2 tbsp sugar until syrupy. Thread 600g chicken thigh pieces onto skewers and grill, basting with the glaze, until sticky and charred. Scatter with spring onion.

m.note: hiding out in the snowy mountain village
m.how: Braise 600g pork belly in soy and water for 2 hours, then slice. Whisk white miso into hot stock. Cook ramen noodles and soft-boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes. Build bowls with pork, halved eggs, nori and spring onion.

w.note: the quiet gardens of the Yashida estate
w.how: Soften 1L vanilla ice cream for 10 minutes. Whisk 2 tbsp matcha powder with a splash of hot water to a paste and fold through until pale green. Refreeze for an hour and scoop into small bowls.

d.note: the funeral and the long night after
d.how: Pour sake into a small jug and stand it in a pot of hot water for 5 minutes until warm. Pour into small cups. For anyone not drinking, brew a pot of green tea instead and serve in the same cups.
